name: Angkor: The invisible city
feature: Orthogonal streets, mounds, canals, ponds and temple precincts extend well beyond the famous stone enclosures.
finding: Airborne laser scans documented urban layout and water infrastructure concealed under vegetation. The findings overturned a temple-only picture of Angkor.
metric: ~1,000 km² extended low-density urban complex (context from published analysis)
evidence: Peer-reviewed LiDAR interpretation; structures and traces supported by surveys, not a complete year-by-year city map
visual: Synthetic orthogonal earthworks and canal-like depressions. No coordinates or elevations are copied from measured LiDAR.

name: Caracol: Roads through jungle
feature: Raised causeways connect monumental precincts; terraces and reservoirs reshape hillsides around dispersed settlement.
finding: A roughly 200 km² airborne LiDAR survey revealed a heavily modified urban landscape beneath the canopy, including features with low relief.
metric: ~200 km² surveyed; low-relief features down to ~5–30 cm discussed in the publication
sourceTitle: Chase et al., Journal of Archaeological Science (2011)
evidence: Measured LiDAR survey and archaeologically interpreted features; not every return has been excavated
visual: Generated radial causeways and stepped terraces; not a measured Caracol DEM.

name: Maya lowlands: The crowded forest
anchor: regional map anchor, not a specific excavation
feature: Dispersed structures, fortified areas, terraces, roads and field systems link urban centers and rural landscapes.
finding: A multi-area survey challenged older assumptions about the scale and density of Maya lowland settlement.
metric: 2,144 km² surveyed; 61,480 ancient structures identified in the reported region
evidence: Peer-reviewed LiDAR synthesis; regional population projections are model-based, not census counts
visual: Synthetic settlement clusters and causeways; no original LiDAR pixels or exact site coordinates reproduced.

name: Campeche: Cities in environmental LiDAR
anchor: broad regional anchor, not the exact location of Valeriana
feature: Environmental LiDAR collected for non-archaeological purposes revealed dense archaeological landscapes and previously unrecorded urbanism.
finding: The study illustrates how 'found' remote-sensing datasets can expose sites that archaeological campaigns had not deliberately targeted.
metric: Previously unrecorded regional urbanism; no exact new-city population asserted here
evidence: Published landscape interpretation. Regional marker intentionally avoids claiming a protected site coordinate.
visual: Generated platform nodes and ponds; not a recovered architectural plan.

name: Casarabe: Cities of the Bolivian Amazon
anchor: approximate regional anchor, not one excavated platform
feature: Monumental platforms, concentric enclosures and roads connect large and small settlement nodes across seasonally inundated lowlands.
finding: The mapping documented a form of pre-Hispanic low-density urbanism in the Bolivian Amazon previously difficult to appreciate from the surface.
metric: ~200 km² of LiDAR mapped across six non-contiguous areas
evidence: Peer-reviewed remote sensing and archaeology; constructed geometry is not surveyed footprint
visual: Generated causeways, platform rectangles and circular ditches, not an exact Casarabe GIS file.
